translationRepairs: His elder brother inherited their father's marquisate; Shi Dan declined any share of the estate.
His elder brother inherited their father's marquisate and declined any share of the estate.

In 丹兄嗣父爵為侯，讓不受分 the continuing subject of 讓不受分 is 丹兄; s0053 丹盡得父財 confirms Shi Dan received the whole estate, so the original attribution of declining the share to Shi Dan is wrong and the proposed repair is accurate.
Dan's elder brother inherited their father's marquisate as marquis; Dan yielded and did not accept a share.
Dan's elder brother inherited their father's marquisate as marquis; he yielded and did not accept a share.
讓不受分 continues the subject 丹兄 from 丹兄嗣父爵為侯; replacing the wrongly inserted subject Dan with he correctly keeps the elder brother as the one who yielded the share, consistent with 丹盡得父財.
Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, came from Wen in Henei commandery. He was the younger brother of Grand Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.
Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, came from Wen in Henei commandery. He was a paternal cousin of Grand Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.
從父弟 denotes a younger paternal cousin (son of a father's brother), not a uterine younger brother; the proposed idiomatic line correctly repairs that kinship without altering other accurate content.
Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, was a man of Wen in Henei; he was the younger brother by the same father of Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.
Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, was a man of Wen in Henei; he was a younger paternal cousin of Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.

從父弟 is a collateral paternal cousin, not a same-father younger brother; younger brother by the same father invents agnatic siblingship that the Chinese does not state, and the proposed literal repair restores the correct kinship.
